name: São Paulo
operatingHours: São Paulo Metro runs ~4:40 AM–midnight daily; CPTM commuter trains ~4:00 AM–midnight. Trains every 2–6 min at peak, 6–10 min late at night. No all-night rail service; night buses (Madrugadão) run after midnight.
fareInfo: Single fare R$5.40 on Metro, CPTM and monorail (2026); city bus R$5.30; bus-to-rail integration R$9.38. Tap a Bilhete Único or a contactless bank card at the gates. A pre-loaded Bilhete Único allows transfers within the integration windows.

sights.name: Ibirapuera Park
sights.note: The city's great urban park, with lakes, jogging tracks, Niemeyer-designed pavilions and several museums among the trees.

sights.name: Avenida Paulista
sights.note: São Paulo's financial and cultural spine, lined with towers, museums and cafés and closed to cars on Sundays for a street party.
sights.hours: Open 24 hours; car-free Sundays ~10:00 AM–6:00 PM

sights.name: Pinacoteca do Estado de São Paulo
sights.note: Brazilian art from the 19th century to today in a restored brick-and-skylight building beside Luz Park.
sights.hours: Wed–Mon 10:00 AM–6:00 PM, closed Tue (free first Sat of the month)

sights.name: Liberdade
sights.note: The world's largest Japanese community outside Japan, with red lanterns, ramen counters, shrines and a weekend street fair.
sights.hours: Streets open daily; fair Sat–Sun ~9:00 AM–7:00 PM

sights.name: MASP (São Paulo Museum of Art)
sights.note: European and Brazilian masterpieces displayed on glass easels in a landmark concrete-and-glass box lifted on red pillars.
sights.hours: Tue 10:00 AM–8:00 PM (free), Wed–Sun 10:00 AM–6:00 PM (Thu to 8:00 PM), closed Mon

sights.name: Mercado Municipal de São Paulo
sights.note: A 1930s market hall with stained-glass windows, famous for the towering mortadella sandwich and the pastel de bacalhau.
sights.hours: Mon–Sat 6:00 AM–6:00 PM, Sun 6:00 AM–4:00 PM

sights.name: Museu Catavento
sights.note: A hands-on science museum for all ages, set in the grand former Palácio das Indústrias.
sights.hours: Tue–Sun 9:00 AM–4:00 PM (last entry), closed Mon

sights.name: Museu do Futebol
sights.note: An interactive museum of Brazilian football inside Pacaembu Stadium, with exhibits on Pelé and the World Cups.
sights.hours: Tue–Sun 9:00 AM–5:00 PM (last entry), closed Mon

sights.name: Mosteiro de São Bento
sights.note: A working Benedictine monastery and basilica downtown, known for its calm interior and Gregorian chant at Sunday Mass.
sights.hours: Daily ~6:00 AM–6:00 PM; chant Mass Sun ~10:00 AM

sights.name: Catedral da Sé
sights.note: A neo-Gothic cathedral with a large dome that anchors the city's zero-kilometre square.

sights.name: Beco do Batman
sights.note: A lane of constantly changing street art in Vila Madalena, ringed by galleries, bars and craft shops.
sights.hours: Open daily; best by day, ~24 hours outdoors

sights.name: Theatro Municipal de São Paulo
sights.note: A 1911 opera house in an ornate Beaux-Arts style, visited by guided tour or a concert.
sights.hours: Guided tours ~Tue–Sat, check the schedule; performances vary

sights.name: Farol Santander
sights.note: A 1930s skyscraper turned cultural centre whose top-floor terrace gives a free-flowing 360-degree view of downtown.

sights.name: Estação da Luz
sights.note: The 1901 British-built railway station with a cast-iron roof and clock tower, still one of the city's busiest transport hubs.
sights.hours: Station open ~4:00 AM–midnight; free to enter

sights.name: Museu da Língua Portuguesa
sights.note: A museum celebrating the Portuguese language through sound, film and installations, housed inside Luz Station.

railStations.name: Luz Station
railStations.note: The city's historic rail hub: CPTM Lines 7-Ruby (to Jundiaí), 10-Turquoise and 11-Coral, plus Metro Lines 1-Blue and 4-Yellow. There is no intercity passenger rail; long-distance travel is by bus from Tietê terminal (Line 1).

airports.name: Guarulhos International Airport
airports.transitNote: CPTM Line 13-Jade (not on this map) runs from Brás to Aeroporto-Guarulhos in ~25–30 min, then a free shuttle bus runs to the terminals; Brás connects to Metro Line 3-Red. Airport buses to Paulista/Tatuapé and taxis (~R$150–200, 45–90 min) are alternatives.
airports.hours: Line 13: first train ~4:00 AM, last ~midnight. Late arrivals: airport buses or ride-share.

airports.name: Congonhas Airport
airports.transitNote: In the city, ~12 km south of Paulista. No direct rail link on this map: take a taxi/ride-share (~20–40 min) or a bus to Line 5-Lilac (Santa Cruz or Moema area) and change. Domestic and shuttle flights (Rio, Brasília, Belo Horizonte).
airports.hours: Metro Line 5-Lilac ~4:40 AM–midnight; taxis and ride-share all hours.
